programs.vm_police_on_all: Start ultrasonic, light and loudness detectors plus Neo mascot/status display; any event triggers the finite police sequence. Requires updated ESP function 269 and /img/Iris_formatted.gif on Neo.
programs.vm_police_on_any_change: Run all three detectors and finite police flashes without requiring Neo or OLED; previous stable fallback.
programs.vm_police_on_sensor_change: Run ultrasonic and dynamic light-change detectors; either event triggers finite police flashes. Light sampling pauses during LED activity.
programs.vm_police_on_ultrasonic_change: Poll 100 mm ultrasonic changes at 250 ms and trigger police flashes; coalesce events while flashing.
programs.vm_police_on_loudness_rise: Trigger police flashes when newer five-second mean loudness is twice older five-second mean, above RMS 20.
programs.vm_police_sequence_vm: Configure two 200 ms LED tracks from VM registers for ten alternating flashes in two seconds; both end off. Native sequence completes after VM halts.
programs.vm_police_lights: Continuous blue/red alternation every 125 ms using LED_EXTERNAL. Stopping VM can leave one LED on; use the finite police sequence normally.
programs.vm_led_blink: Continuous onboard RGB LED blink with a dim green value of 8 and 500 ms steps; stopping VM may leave its last state.
programs.vm_ultrasonic_change_start: Start the native ultrasonic detector at 250 ms with a 100 mm delta, then halt. Stop the native thread explicitly when finished.
programs.vm_light_change_start: Start dynamic light-change detection at 250 ms with a 200-count margin, then halt; baseline comes from current readings.
programs.vm_mic_rise_start: Start the rolling ten-bucket loudness detector at 200% ratio and minimum RMS 20, then halt. Missing HALT fixed during catalog review.
programs.vm_sound_capture: Measure MIC_ABOVE with threshold 50; capture JPEG after a loud sample, wait three seconds, then resume polling at 250 ms. Writes SD photos.
programs.vm_sound_capture_test: Same sound/camera flow with RMS threshold 1; controlled integration fixture only, can repeatedly write photos.
programs.vm_camera_once: Capture one numbered JPEG to ESP SD and halt; sequence number is returned in r0.
programs.vm_camera_sequence: Start the native five-photo sequence with one-second intervals; sequence continues after VM halts. Writes SD JPEGs.
programs.vm_storage_mic: Read SD capacity into r0 and microphone RMS into r1, then halt; no test files created.
programs.vm_audio_one_second: Record a one-second PCM WAV to ESP SD; sample count is returned in r1. Writes an audio file.
programs.vm_video_one_second: Retired: calls removed CAMERA_VIDEO (107) to make two-frame MJPEG. Do not run on cleaned-up firmware; use camera sequences and Neo assembly.
programs.vm_dht11_once: Wait 2100 ms for DHT11 startup, read temperature plus humidity detail, then halt.
programs.vm_light_once: Read current photoresistor ADC with the default sample count and halt; r0 contains the reading.
programs.vm_radio_status: Read Wi-Fi status into r0 and BLE connection state into r1, then halt; no scan or reconfiguration.
programs.vm_rssi_ten_seconds: Retired: uses removed RSSI_ON/OFF (112/113). Use vm_rssi_scan and the common sampling thread instead.
programs.vm_rssi_scan: Start the default ten-second native RSSI scan thread; snapshots are saved as timestamped SD CSV files.
programs.vm_ir_scan: Start the default ten-second native IR capture thread. A known remote/source is needed to verify reception; it does not replay IR.
programs.vm_ir_transmit_sequence: Start five short carrier bursts using the native IR sequence. Emits IR; requires an explicit receiver/target fixture.
programs.vm_env_thread: Start continuous temperature/humidity sampling every 2500 ms, saving timestamped SD CSV files; explicitly stop the thread when finished.

common_programs.arithmetic: Compute 7 + 5 into r2 and halt; hardware-independent VM smoke test.
common_programs.time_now: Read logical monotonic milliseconds into r0 and halt; no timer reset.
common_programs.time_reset: Reset the logical timer to zero and halt; changes timestamps used by running programs, so test in isolation.
